terms.gloss: a horse chestnut (the nut, and the tree)
terms.grammar: castanea, castaneae f. with the adjective equīnus, equīna, equīnum
terms.comment: The tree (Aesculus hippocastanum) came to western Europe only in the sixteenth century and has no ancient name; the botanists’ Latin of that time calls it the “horse chestnut”, as most modern languages still do. Both words are classical: castanea the sweet chestnut, equīnus “of horses”. For the edible chestnut see “chestnut”; for the acorn see “acorn”.

phrases.english: It’s a conker; don’t eat it.
What a lot of conkers we’ve collected!

sources: Lewis & Short: castanea · Lewis & Short: equinus
